text.p: National-Standard Co said Thursday it is restructuring its United Kingdom operations and taking a $9.9 million charge to cover the cost of staff cuts and inventory and fixed asset write-offs.

The company said it is cutting 124 of the 345 jobs and discontinuing the Copperply wire and certain weld wire product lines. Headcount reductions will save $3 million a year. Annual sales will be reduced to $30 million from $37 million.
National-Standard, which makes a variety of wire-related products, reported a fiscal second quarter loss of $2.03, including the charge, versus a profit of $0.28 a year ago.
Cash outlays during the next 12 months included in the $9.9 million are expected to be $2.7 million. Cash outlays expected beyond the next 12 months are approximately $3.0 million.

"In spite of significant efforts over the past few years to improve the UK operating results, the operation has not achieved the level of contribution to increasing stakeholder value that National-Standard expects from its business units," Michael Savitske, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Year-to-date, National-Standard said its UK subsidiary has lost $1.4 million, compared with losses of $300,000 during the first six months last year. In the past 12 months, the UK operation has reported losses of $2.3 million.
Prior to the restructuring, the UK unit had lost $5.3 million since 1993. Without the change, National-Standard said the losses would continue.
"Going forward, our goal is to establish an economically viable business that will generate positive value for our stakeholders," said Savitske.
